subject.title: [Feature]: Standardize skill data directory convention (configPaths) under ~/.openclaw/

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class per-skill writable data directory, and should that contract be a filesystem convention, a plugin/skill SDK API, or ClawHub authoring guidance?
rationale: The request creates durable storage and metadata semantics for third-party skills, which affects compatibility, security boundaries, backups, and the core-vs-ClawHub ownership split.

options.title: Design A Generic Core Contract
options.body: Keep this open and specify a stable state-dir or SDK-backed skill data contract with docs, install behavior, and upgrade expectations before implementation.

options.title: Route To ClawHub Guidance
options.body: Treat this as a skill publishing convention and document/package it through ClawHub unless a missing OpenClaw API is identified.

options.title: Use Existing Config Only
options.body: Decline a new filesystem convention and steer skill authors to `skills.entries.<key>.config` or plugin-owned storage where appropriate.

recommendation.title: Design A Generic Core Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this open and specify a stable state-dir or SDK-backed skill data contract with docs, install behavior, and upgrade expectations before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans skills, ClawHub, state-directory policy, and public metadata/API boundaries, where steipete has the strongest current routing history.
